law: CFString objects are immutable—use to create and manage a string that can be changed after it has been created.
The specified range must not exceed the length of the string.

You should never, though, store a hash value outside of your application and expect it to be useful if you read it back in later (hash values may change between different releases of the operating system).
(Note that arrays can’t contain pointers; in most cases, though, you can use the constant instead.) Values are not copied but retained using the retain callback provided when an array was created.
